title: Entering a group dims the layer list but not the canvas
detail: SPLIT, and the two halves went opposite ways. The canvas half STAYS OPEN as a decision, not a bug: the dim was declined because opacity is in Fabric stateProperties, so dimming the canvas would serialise view state into every save, which §67 forbids. That reasoning still holds and nothing here overturns it. The layer half was not a decision at all but a defect, and it was worse than this row says — the row recorded that the list dims today (data-context=false), which is true only after something unrelated re-projects the tree. Fixed as vg-058.

title: The line chart occasionally slides left as if correcting a position
detail: NOT REPRODUCED in 30 seconds of live playback against a real host, and BOTH of the rows named candidates are ruled out for that window. The row guessed a resize observer re-fitting mid-animation, or a chart settling after a viewport change; neither fired: the viewport transform was byte-identical at the start and the end (0.61602870 with the same offset, zero changes in thirty samples), the chart own box never moved (left 616, top 695, 963x215, angle 0, scale 1 and 1), and a ResizeObserver on the body fired once, which is the probe own DOM reads rather than anything the chart did. STILL OPEN, because occasionally is rarer than thirty seconds and closing it on a non-reproduction would be the same mistake as filing it on a screenshot. WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD USE, because two attempts here failed for one reason and the reason is worth keeping: counting ink in the chart region cannot see this. The card is opaque and the sampled rect includes the dark part of the backdrop, so every column reads as drawn and every column reads as dark — the first probe reported a constant firstX of 0 and lastX of the full width, and a luminance profile reported the same. Watching the EVENTS is what separates a slide from data changing, because data moves locally and a slide moves everything.

title: The preview data source fluctuates faster than a real PC
detail: "The Preview data source fluctuate too rapidly which is not realistic to a normal PC hardware behavior, and a bit distracting for the author." The cadence is a number in fake-source. 'Realistic' needs a decision about what the preview is for.

title: The top bar becomes a toolbar of icon buttons on the theme document, and its commands are renamed
detail: "The top bar menu is kinda lost in direction of what's it for. Some are legitimate functions you can't find anywhere else (File & View menus), but Edit & Insert is a duplication of actions that already in their rightful places. Verdict: Make it an actual toolbar (icon buttons, not nested inside a menu) with actions to the theme document, not individual elements." AND the rename, in full: Save Package -> Activate (instructs the player to switch to this theme); Release Package -> Export theme; Open Package -> Import theme; Open library -> Open; Save to library -> Save; ADD a Save as button; New from starter -> New from template (only one template today, more are coming). Note Activate and Save as are missing capabilities, not renames: the host already stores the active theme and the theme route is a PUT to a named id, so each is one id away. Do this as one change, not seven renamings — the Arrange menu was already removed on exactly this reasoning (vg-016), and doing the buttons without the toolbar shape means doing the work twice.

title: Should the editor be rebuilt on Base UI + shadcn/ui + Tailwind before further micro-adjustments?
detail: "Honestly the entire editor UI is kind of boring, primitive & unpolish... Should we do a whole redesign of it with Base UI - Shadcn - TailwindCSS, which has been in the queue long enough, before doing any micro adjustments to specific UI details? I'm talking about the whole panels rearrangement, too." The same question as vg-031 one level up, and the same wrong answer: the ecosystem search was run against Base UI alone. FIRST STEP IS NOT A REDESIGN — it is searching shadcn/ui for the panels this editor already has (dialog, select, tabs, popover, tooltip, slider, switch, scroll-area, separator) and finding out which replace hand-rolled equivalents. Then bring the result back to choose: full redesign first, or defect fixes first. Bigger than any other item here and deliberately unstarted.

title: A desktop-shaped theme letterboxes to 31% of a phone's height
detail: MEASURED: the stress fixture at 412x839 gives an artboard of about 412x258 with bars above and below. Nothing overflows, nothing is cropped, no console errors — this is contain working exactly as §53 specifies. Filed because two rulings pull against each other and only the user can settle which wins: "a phone is the main display type" and "content is always contain" cannot both be satisfied by a desktop-shaped theme on a portrait phone, because the content will be whole and the text about 6px. Three ways out — leave it, add a per-display fit, or let a theme declare the size it is designed for — and which one is right depends on who reads these displays and from how far.

title: The line chart's Glass control: a Circle's frost reads stronger than a Rect's at the same value
detail: RULING STANDS: a slight per-shape difference is acceptable rather than no glass on closed shapes; the expensive option wins by default. CHARACTERISED, NOT FIXED, and the lead I gave the investigator was wrong. I offered "the Circle region measured 127,449 px against the Rect 156,009 for the same box" as proof the region was shape-dependent. It is not: that sweep gave every shape the same AUTHORING box, and a Circle has no 240x160. Both numbers reconstruct exactly at the sweep pad — 437x357 = 156,009 and 357x357 = 127,449, predicted ratio 0.8165 against 0.81691 measured. At one 260x260 box all five shapes take a byte-identical 362x362 region (131,044 px). PARTIAL COVERAGE REFUTED: no collapse at the rim, and the bin touching the boundary is the largest bin in three of four measurements. MATERIAL PARITY IS BIT-IDENTICAL: mean luma 94.75/94.75 over stripes and 93.41/93.41 over a photograph, distinct colours 40/40 and 10/10, and the frost boxes are pixel-identical at thresholds 2, 1.5 and 1. WHAT DIFFERS IS FOOTPRINT: a Circle covers 78.54% of its box, 21.5% less frosted area — which reads LIGHTER, not stronger, so it is the wrong direction to explain the report. STILL OPEN, and the leading hypothesis is not the renderer: a Circle authored size is a RADIUS and a Rect authored size is a WIDTH, so the same number gives a disc twice the area. Checked and not yet confirmed in the scene where it was seen. glass.ts is byte-identical to the base sha; nothing was simulated away, per the ruling. THE AUTHORS PATH TO THIS COMPARISON IS REACHABLE AFTER ALL, and I said otherwise earlier and was wrong twice about it. First: I claimed the Glass blur control does not exist on a chart. It does not exist on a chart because a chart cannot be frosted — the control appears once there is a radius to tune, and I compared an object that was refused against one that already had frost on. Second: I then said the report could not have come from the editor because the line charts control cannot be changed. True, and beside the point: the report is about a CIRCLE and a RECT, and both are perfectly authorable. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY SHAPE, which is also the ruling ADR-0015 predicts: Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon all offer an ENABLED Frosted glass control; Polyline and Line are aria-disabled, correctly, having no closed area to frost. And the two shapes the report names get the SAME DEFAULT: a fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both become vigiliaGlass at blurRadius 16 the moment frost is switched on, with the blur control appearing alongside it. So the situation the report describes — a Circle and a Rect at the same value — is exactly what the product produces by default, and the row stands on its own merits again. What remains is what the earlier characterisation established and this does not change: over the area they share the frost is bit-identical, and what differs is footprint, a Circle covering 78.54 percent of its box. If a Circle reads stronger, the leading hypothesis is still the authors own — a Circle size is a RADIUS where a Rectangle size is a WIDTH — and it is still unconfirmed in the scene where it was seen.
check: Measured across every shape in the running editor: Frosted glass is enabled on Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon, and aria-disabled on Polyline and Line with the reason on focus. A fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both take blurRadius 16 on the same click, and the Glass blur control appears only after that.

title: Auto-save, and a prompt for recovery after a browser crash
detail: RULED: draft in browser storage; write on a ~30 s timer and on leaving the page; recovery offers restore-or-discard naming what was lost; and the editor opens a theme from the library, which is the seam the other two need. BLOCKED: the asset-ownership question decides where the draft lives — if the editor stops holding asset bytes and the host owns them, the draft is a host write and browser storage is wrong.

title: What is derived state in a persisted Fabric object?
detail: The dirty guard's cause (vg-026) is one field of a general question, and patching styles alone leaves the next per-character cache to arrive and be found by the user. SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES is an allowlist that already intends to do this job and is not applied on the way out. The spec should answer which Fabric properties are derived from telemetry or from rendering, how a serialisation excludes all of them, and whether the allowlist should be enforced at the boundary. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-asset-ownership.md. AND NOW THERE IS A SHARP INSTANCE OF IT, MEASURED, which is vg-026. The dirty guard compares a document key against one captured when the editor was built, and with no input at all 13 of the Starter 52 objects change between 0.4 and 1.9 seconds after load — every one a Textbox, repainted by the live preview pass. The document differs from itself with nothing touched, so every New asks the author to save work nobody did. That is what the allowlist was meant to stop and does not reach: the changed objects are bound text, and what the live pass writes is the same property the author edits. This row is therefore not an abstract design question any more — it is one concrete false prompt an author meets on the first Ctrl+N, and the fix belongs here rather than in the dirty guard.

title: The artboard is not a clipping area, and neither repair is free
detail: Fabric has no scene-level clip: clipPath is per-object and serialised through cacheProperties, so it collides with the crop manager's authored per-image clip and with the derived text-box clip. Two candidate repairs, both with consequences — a scene Group wrapper changes what canvas.getObjects() means, which is the layer tree's and every walk over it. A decision, not a patch. Related: a selection handle should stay fully visible when its object is clipped (the user's own requirement in the same report).

title: Where the defect queue lives: the open-ended pass, the Superpowers lifecycle, and beads
detail: The working-out of whether every defect should become a spec and a plan (overkill), and where an open-ended queue sits beside a change lifecycle that has a finish line. Beads is proven installable natively on Windows (v1.3.0, no WSL) with the full lifecycle exercised; bd init edits AGENTS.md and installs hooks by default and --skip-agents declines that. Marked undecided by the user pending thought — specifically, not wanting two agent frameworks fighting each other. The registry is the incumbent until this is decided.

title: The layer list cannot select more than one row, and grouping needs a multi-selection
detail: The row click is onClick={() => selectLayer(row.id)} and ignores the event, so a shift-click on a second row replaces the first instead of adding to it. MEASURED: shift-clicking strapline after wordmark left only strapline selected, while the same two objects shift-clicked on the canvas select both. Grouping is reachable — the context menu offers Group once the selection is eligible — but only from a canvas multi-selection, so an author working in the layer list cannot make one. Needs a decision rather than a patch: whether a shift-click toggles a row the way the canvas does, whether shift extends a range like a file list, or whether the panel stays single-select and grouping moves somewhere reachable from it. An additive select also has to cross the Fabric-free bridge, which has one selectLayer(id) today.

title: Reopening the editor discards saved work and shows the Starter instead
detail: MEASURED THREE WAYS, and it is the second half of vg-059's damage. Rename the theme through the theme-settings Name field from System dashboard to SENTINEL-9931 - the field reads SENTINEL-9931 and the host's document reads {"name":"SENTINEL-9931"}. Then reload the editor page. The Name field reads System dashboard again and the layer list is the Starter's 52 rows. The saved work is still on the host - it is the editor that does not open it. So the author's round trip is: edit, see it saved, close the tab, reopen, and be holding the Starter with no prompt and no warning that what they were working on is still there. NOT THE SAME AS vg-026: that row is the discard prompt appearing when it should not, and this is a document that never being loaded in the first place, so even discarding everything correctly would not help. THE ACTIVE THEME IS UNSET, which is where I would look first but have not established: /api/themes/active returns {"active":null} alongside the theme list, so nothing designates vigilia-demo-dashboard as what the editor should open, and Save to library evidently does not set it. Save to library, Release package and Open package are three different verbs in the File menu and only one of them is the one an author means by save. Worth noting for whoever picks this up: the editor does reach the library through File > Open library, so the path exists - what is missing is that the default open is the Starter rather than the author's own theme, and that Open library first raises the same spurious Save changes before opening another theme prompt that vg-026 is about. RE-CONFIRMED AT ITS STRONGEST, with the editor rebuilt and on the current mainline, and this time the work is a real object rather than a name. Rename the theme to MY-REAL-WORK, insert a Rectangle, File > Save to library: the host's document reads MY-REAL-WORK with 53 objects - the Starter's 52 plus the rectangle. Then reload the editor, which is what closing and reopening the tab does. The Name field reads System dashboard and the layer list shows 52 rows. The author's name is gone, their rectangle is gone, and nothing was said. This is the shape an author actually loses work in, and it is the same shape vg-071 makes invisible: there is no dirty marker to warn them before the reload (vg-071) and the reload itself discards the theme they were working on (this row). Together they are a session's work vanishing with no signal at either end. NOT THE DISCARD PROMPT and not the Starter's dirty-on-open state that vg-026 is about - I re-checked that guard this pass and it is correct, Ctrl+N on an untouched document goes straight to the size dialog and the prompt appears only after a real edit. The defect here is narrower and worse: the default document the editor opens is the template, not the author's own saved theme, and no part of the product says so.

title: The editor never says an object has fallen outside the artboard, but the player counts them precisely
detail: MEASURED AS A CONTRAST BETWEEN THE TWO SURFACES, which is what makes it a defect rather than a missing nicety. In the editor, type 700 into the theme-settings Width field and 400 into Height - the canvas zooms to 199% and 44 of the 52 objects are now outside the artboard. The editor says nothing. Its entire off-artboard vocabulary is one static sentence that is present at every size and never changes: Objects are not moved or resized. Anything outside the artboard is not shown on a display. No count, no badge, no highlighted layer row, no status-bar line, and /outside|off.?canvas|clipped/i matches exactly that one sentence. Save to library and open the player on the same document, and it says: 44 of 52 objects are outside this artboard and are not shown - past the right edge and past the bottom edge. Same document, same host, same numbers, and the surface an author can act in is the silent one. The direction is the part that should be hard to reproduce by accident: naming the right edge and the bottom edge means the player already computes which side each object fell off, and that per-object answer is exactly what an author needs to fix the layout. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING. The editor is where the mistake is made and the only place it can be undone, and it is the one surface that does not know the mistake happened. Worth noting the player earns its keep here - this is not a case for adding a warning to a display, it is a case for the author not having to go and look at a display to find out. The count and the edge names are already computed; nothing new needs deciding about how to say it, only where to say it.

title: A pasted image is saved as a blob: URL and never becomes an asset, so it is gone everywhere else
detail: MEASURED END TO END, AND IT IS SILENT DATA LOSS. Put a PNG on the clipboard, click the canvas, press Ctrl+V. The image appears on the canvas at 0,0, is named Image, and the inspector shows it with a Crop button - the paste path itself works. Then File > Save to library. The saved document does contain an object named Image, and its src reads blob:http://127.0.0.1:5311/081c983e-cebf-4fd8-b75a-8d9a3e45bfc8. A blob URL is a handle into one browser session's memory; it means nothing in any other tab, any other browser, on a phone, or on a second visit.  HALF FIXED, AND THE REAL BLOCKER IS NOW NAMED. A pasted image took the HALF-ONLY PATH: the clipboard called imageManager.importImage and stopped, so the object kept the blob URL it was decoded from and nothing ever declared the bytes. The assets pane did both halves and the paste did not, which is why an asset import survives and a paste does not. AssetManager now owns both — placeImage declares the file AND puts it on the canvas — and the assets pane and a paste both go through it, so neither can take the half-only path again. The clipboard manager takes its importer from the session, which owns the asset manager; the shell builds it before that exists, so the importer is installed rather than injected. MEASURED on a pasted PNG: the saved envelope now declares assets/pasted-probe.png and the object carries vigiliaAsset {assetId pasted-probe, kind image}, which it did not before. STILL BROKEN, and this is the part that matters: the objects src STILL serialises as blob:http://... because NOTHING IN THE RENDERER RESOLVES vigiliaAsset. Searched every reader — the asset manager uses it to count references and to refuse removal, and scene-fabric only writes and reads it as a property; no adapter, scene or player path turns an assetId into a URL. So the bytes now ship and the image still does not travel, and the remaining fix is not in the editor at all: the scene has to resolve the reference the way it already resolves background media through createAssetResolver. Until that exists, a pasted image is a session handle with a copy of its bytes attached. Editor suite 1055 across 86 files.
check: Live on a pasted PNG: the envelope declares assets/pasted-probe.png and the object carries vigiliaAsset {assetId pasted-probe, kind image}; before, neither existed. The src is still a blob URL and no renderer path resolves the reference, which is the remaining half and is recorded as such.
owner: scene-fabric (the resolver); editor paste path is done

title: Nothing anywhere says the document has unsaved changes
detail: MEASURED BY HUNTING FOR A SIGNAL THAT IS NOT THERE, which is the only way to measure an absence. There is a dedicated status element for it - footer.editor-shell-status, reading Fabric editor ready - so the affordance exists and is wired to something. It never changes. Select an object: still Fabric editor ready. Save to library: still Fabric editor ready. Type into the theme Name field and leave it unsaved, giving the document a real difference from what is on disk: still Fabric editor ready. Alongside it, the document title is Vigilia — editor with no asterisk and no suffix, no element carries a class matching /dirty|unsaved|modified/i anywhere in the tree, and the body text contains no unsaved marker. So an author who has just renamed their theme and typed a rectangle has no visible signal that anything is pending. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC COMPLAINT IS THE COMBINATION WITH vg-060, and the two together are worse than either alone. vg-060 is that reopening the editor loads the Starter rather than the saved theme, so saved work disappears from view on reload. This is that nothing tells the author work is pending before they reload. An author renames a theme, adds a card, sees no dirty marker, closes the tab, reopens, and is looking at the Starter - with two independent signals that should have prevented it and neither present. There is a dirty key in the editor already: vg-026's own description records that isDirty is a string comparison against a key captured in the PersistenceManager constructor, and the Ctrl+N prompt consults it at editor-session.ts. So the state exists and is read in one place; it is simply never surfaced. The cheapest version of this fix is the status line the editor already has. ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED, because the fix does not work and the reason is worth the row. The obvious signal is save() in editor-shell, which is what every OBJECT manager calls, so I plumbed a document-change callback from it to the status bar and rendered Unsaved changes over the last message. Live, the status did not move: a nudge still read Fabric editor ready, and renaming the theme in the Name field still read Fabric editor ready, while Save to library correctly read Saved to library. So save() is NOT the funnel the rows hunt-by-hunting-for-a-signal assumed. There are at least THREE edit paths — object managers through save(), the nudge through the shortcut manager into canvas-nudge, and the theme and palette fields through their own panels commits — and only the first goes through it. The reason it matters: PersistenceManager.isDirty(current, assets) already answers this exactly, and the session already calls it, but only on the way to a replacement prompt. Wiring every edit path would duplicate a comparison that already exists; asking the session for the answer instead is the design question, not a patch. Reverted rather than shipped: a status bar that says Fabric editor ready while dirty would be worse than the current one, which at least says nothing false.
owner: editor/src/persistence-manager (the answer exists); the wiring is the design question

title: The editor still does not refit the theme when the window is resized
detail: FILED SEPARATELY BECAUSE IT SURVIVED THE FIX FOR vg-068, and measured by hand rather than taken from the agent's report. Open the editor at 2048 wide and the zoom badge reads 83%. Resize the window to 1600 and it reads 83%; to 1280, still 83%; to 1024, still 83%. One number across a 1024-pixel change, while the canvas behind it goes 1394, 946, 626, 370. Click Zoom to fit at that last size and the badge reads 22% - so the fit calculation is right and something else has to ask for it. THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES IT IS WHICH EVENT FIRES THE REFIT. cde9aa6 made a PANEL COLLAPSE refit, and that works: at 1024, hiding the layer panel takes the canvas 370 to 658 and the zoom 22% to 39%. A WINDOW RESIZE is a different event and did not get the same treatment. This is the half that matters in ordinary use, because a deliberate panel toggle is rare and resizing a window - or opening it at a size and keeping it - is what everyone does. An author whose window is not the width they opened the editor at spends the session looking at a theme at the wrong zoom inside a black field, and the badge reads a confident number throughout. Nothing recomputes on resize; only the click recomputes it. A ResizeObserver already exists on the body in this app for other purposes, so the seam is present. ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED, and the reason it was reverted is the useful part. CONFIRMED EXACTLY AS FILED: at 2048 the badge reads 83% with the canvas at 1394; resize to 1024 and it still reads 83% with the canvas at 370, and the artboard still starts at x 98, so 1290 of its 1388 pixels run off the right edge. Zoom to fit at that size gives 22%, so the fit exists — it is just not automatic. THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG. Holding the zoom and re-centring the translation on every resize does exactly what the row wants — measured, at 370 the board then spans -512 to 882 against a 370 canvas, so it is centred and the rest is reachable by panning — and it BREAKS keeps the point under the cursor fixed while zooming, which resize() calls on construction and on every host size change. Panning to inspect a corner and then any resize, spurious or not, yanks the camera back to centre. That test failing is the finding, not an accident of the harness. So the question is not how to re-centre but WHEN: only when the camera was showing the whole board, so an authors pan survives and a fitted view follows the window. That needs a condition on the previous camera state — was it fitted or contained — which the viewport does not currently keep. Reverted rather than shipped: a camera that cannot be left where the author put it is a worse defect than one that leaves part of the board off the edge.

title: Drop the Circle and Triangle shape kinds; a new Ellipse is a circle by default
detail: RULED BY THE USER after measuring the pairs. The premise was checked and holds: nothing in the editor constrains a Circle to stay round. Fabric keeps a Circle radius in step with scaleX and scaleY, so dragging one corner stretches it into an ellipse, and the selection inspector says so itself — a circle, an ellipse and a triangle own NO shape-specific field, each is fully described by the width and height the general fields already carry. So a Circle protects nothing the author cannot undo with one number, and a 3-sided Polygon already reaches a Triangle (MIN_POLYGON_SIDES is 3 with a side-count field). Removing both leaves one entry for each behaviour: an Ellipse that may be round, and a Polygon that may be a triangle. A new Ellipse gets rx === ry, so the common case — a dot, a ring, a chip — is still what you get by default and the round shape is still one click away.

title: The browser will refresh or close with unsaved work and warn nobody
detail: RAISED BY THE USER, and confirmed by hand including a control that proves the measurement is sound rather than an automation blind spot. Select a palette token, click Import asset, choose one file - a real, unsaved change - then refresh. The page goes, 53 rows become 52, and nothing is said: no dialog, no status message, no prompt. Same on navigating away to another page. The obvious worry is that Chromium suppresses beforeunload dialogs under automation, which would make this unmeasurable here rather than absent. It is not: with a beforeunload handler installed by hand on the same page and the same harness, the reload DOES produce a dialog of type beforeunload and the harness records it. So the instrument can see exactly what the app is not producing, and the app produces none. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE OBVIOUS: vg-060 already established that reopening the editor loads the Starter rather than the saved theme, and vg-071 that nothing anywhere signals unsaved work. This is the third leg of the same shape, and it is the one that is nearly free to fix - a beforeunload listener reading the isDirty key the editor already computes. Note the browser owns that dialog's wording and gives no room to customise it, so if the product wants to say what would be lost rather than just ask, that is a deliberate design call rather than something beforeunload can do. Related: vg-071 and vg-060.

title: The colour picker jumps to the top-left of the window the moment it is clicked
detail: RAISED BY THE USER and reproduced exactly, with the coordinates. Open the palette, select Frosted panel, click Pick a colour. The picker opens where it should: 208 by 296 at (1773, 455), anchored beside the swatch that opened it in the right-hand panel. Click once anywhere inside it - the saturation square, which is the control an author reaches for first - and the picker's bounding box is (0, 6). Top-left corner of the window, full 2048 pixels away from where it was and roughly 1773 from the control that owns it. It stays there through subsequent clicks on hue and alpha. THE CONSEQUENCE IS WORSE THAN THE MOVEMENT. The panel now sits over the layer list on the far side of the window, so the controls and the colour they are editing are in different parts of the screen, and the swatch that opened it is off in the inspector with nothing pointing back to the panel that is now editing it. The screenshot at the moment of the jump shows the picker floating over the left rail while the Colour field it is driving reads #0a16234d on the far right. A picker that relocates on its first interaction is not merely misplaced - the author loses the link between what they are dragging and what it is changing, and on a laptop at a smaller window the jump can also push it partly off screen. Nothing here about where it should go is arguable: anchored, and not moving, is what every other colour control does.

title: Selecting a colour stutters badly: nine main-thread stalls across one drag
detail: RAISED BY THE USER as visible lag and stuttering when selecting colours, and measured rather than taken on trust - with the honest caveat that it does not reproduce on every run, which is itself part of what makes it hard to pin down. MEASURED, dragging the saturation square at roughly a human cadence - 20 moves with 40 ms between them, 3.05 seconds of dragging: nine long tasks, durations 93, 68, 76, 50, 81, 60, 77, 88 and 59 milliseconds, totalling 652 ms, maximum 93. That is 21% of the drag time with the main thread blocked, and the stalls are spread across the drag rather than bunched, so the author feels every few pixels. It was measured on Frosted panel, which eight objects use, so one colour change re-renders eight frosted surfaces - the likely shape of the cost, though I did NOT establish that: repeating the drag on tokens with 1, 8 and 28 uses produced no long tasks at all in that run, so the scaling is unconfirmed and the cause is not established here. WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW ANYWAY: this is the interaction an author repeats most in the palette panel, a deliberate drag rather than a click, so per-move cost is exactly the wrong thing to be expensive. It also composes with vg-080 - the picker is already jumping under the author's cursor, and now the drag stutters as well, so the two together make the colour control feel broken rather than merely awkward. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the same drag measured on a token with few uses against Frosted panel's eight, a few runs each, since one clean run and one clean run that measured nothing is not yet a comparison.

title: The gradient control is confusing to use, and it discards the colour it replaces
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - the gradient control is very confusing to use - which is a judgement I am recording rather than contradicting, and which one measurement sharpens rather than settles. WHAT I COULD MEASURE is what the control does to an author's existing work. Select the Frosted panel token, which is a 30% alpha #0815234d used by eight objects, and switch Paint from Solid to Linear gradient. The panel gives Angle, Stop 1 position, Stop 1 colour, Stop 2 position, Stop 2 colour and Add stop, and it is usable - I typed 8-digit hex into a stop and it saved and rendered exactly - so this is not a report of a broken control. What it does is replace the token's colour with #ffffff and #000000, both fully opaque, and both defaults are unlike the colour they are replacing: a 30% frosted panel becomes an opaque black-to-white sweep across eight objects, from one dropdown choice, with the previous colour gone and only undo to get it back. The token row does say Frosted panel · 8, so the author has the count, and the defaults are a defensible starting point. But a gradient seeded with white and black is a colour nobody would have chosen for a frosted panel, and the control offers no starting-from-current behaviour, which is the one thing that would make it feel predictable. THE COMFUSION THE USER DESCRIBED MAY BE EXACTLY THIS and is worth naming rather than assuming: the first thing the control does to a colour is overwrite it with two unrelated colours. That is a design answer, not a defect, and it is the user's call - but the measurement is what an author meets first, and seeding from the current value costs nothing.
